- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.6) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast is above recent high, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.3), reduce forecast lag by 1–3 days to reflect sentiment reversal.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; cap forecast peak at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment is neutral or cooling.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 68–70), reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is weak or volatile, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid overfitting to recent trends.
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., <0.3) and forecast is rising, cap forecast at 1–2% above recent low to avoid false breakout.
